notes: Labeling mode: in-session LLM analysis by model 'glm-5.3' (Augur Step 3 is agent-agnostic; the agent's own model performs the labeling; no external LLM API call was made). 3 batches, 32 candidates total (4 source rows from sources.csv, 28 sink rows from sinks.csv); every CSV candidate was processed, none deferred; batch records with verbatim candidate rows are in labels_raw_pass1.json.

Source-extraction recall gap (verified root cause): extraction/sources.ql family 1 (route_param) emitted ZERO rows, so sources.csv holds only the 4 flask.request.* rows while detection.json expectedVolume predicted 7 (including the route_param rows for put_file/head_file/get_file). Verified with read-only diagnostics in iris/diagnostics (codeql query run, CLI 2.25.1, python-all 7.1.2 pack sources): flaskRouteHandler casts Function.getADecorator() to Attribute, but for the parameterized decorators @app.route("/<path:path>", methods=[...]) (xhu.py:104/:189/:214) getADecorator() returns the decorator CALL node (instanceof Call holds, instanceof Attribute fails); the verified fix pattern is dec.(Call).getFunc().(Attribute).getName() = "route", which matches all four handlers. Phase 2 must add the three route handler parameters (xhu.py:105/:190/:215, parameter `path`) to MySources.qll or Pass1_PathTraversal.ql will produce zero alerts despite the sink labels - flagged as the top human review point.

Sanitizer list is deliberately EMPTY: the only guard, sanitized_join's startswith prefix check (xhu.py:44), compares the un-normalized string of (root / path).absolute(); pathlib.Path.absolute() performs no '..' normalization and no symlink resolution, and the Werkzeug path converter always yields a relative string, so the prefix condition is textually satisfied by every converter-supplied path - the guard does not confine '../' traversal and must not become an isBarrier. Consequently Step 6's generic 'explicit startswith guard -> FP' heuristic must NOT be applied to this target's findings without checking for normalization.

Trust asymmetry: only put_file authenticates its input (HMAC-SHA256 over '{path} {length}' with the operator SECRET_KEY, xhu.py:118-130); head_file and get_file are unauthenticated, so the read-side traversal flows (sink-013 open, sink-026 stat, sink-028 send_file) are the highest-exploitability paths. PUT-side sinks (sink-019, sink-020, sink-023, sink-024) require an HMAC signed over the exact traversal path by the key holder.

Read-side traversal scope is constrained by get_paths' textual suffixes: arbitrary read/stat is limited to file names ending in '.data' (send_file/stat) or '.meta' (open) - recorded in the sink rationales; directory creation (sink-023) is not suffix-constrained.

Independence: no PyVul ground truth, CVE advisories or patch diffs were consulted; the pre-existing audit artifacts in the source-tree root (VULNERABILITY_AUDIT_REPORT.md, path_traversal_sinks.csv, 漏洞审查报告.md, 第一步筛选报告.md) were NOT opened. Labeling used only xhu.py, setup.py, config.example.py, the Phase-1 CSVs, exploration/detection.json and the Augur references (WORKFLOW.md, references/patterns.md, references/python.md, references/flask.md, assets/labels_schema.json).

Diagnostics were run read-only (codeql query run + bqrs decode against the existing database; outputs under iris/diagnostics/). No modification of the source tree, the CodeQL database, the Augur installation, or the Phase-1 original CSVs.

entries.rationale: Genuine untrusted input boundary: the PUT query-string verification key 'v' read via flask.request.args.get (request args are fully attacker-controlled in a Flask/Werkzeug service). Labeled source for pass-1 recall because request-arg values are potential path carriers in Flask apps generally. Input controllability: full (any query-string bytes, URL-decoded by the framework). In THIS codebase the value flows only into hmac.compare_digest (xhu.py:125) as the offered key and is never used as or concatenated into a filesystem path, so it cannot seed a path-traversal flow here; reachability recorded so Phase-2 alert expectations stay accurate.

Labeled summary (parameter 0 -> return taint step) so this propagation survives query generation. It is NOT a sink (performs no file access itself) and - decisively - NOT a sanitizer: the startswith guard at :44 compares str((root / path).absolute()) lexically; pathlib.Path.absolute() performs no '..' normalization and no symlink resolution (CPython: 'Make the path absolute, without normalization or resolving symlinks'), and the Werkzeug path converter always yields a relative string, so the textual prefix condition is satisfied by every converter-supplied path including '../' traversal segments, which the OS then resolves at open/stat/mkdir/send_file time outside DATA_ROOT. Marking this function a barrier would suppress the genuine traversal flow.
